module_name: Influence Maximization, Bots, Trolls, and Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
module_description: Module 18 is the trust-and-safety analytics module: identifying coordinated behavior (co-tweeting, co-posting, synchronized timing), bot and troll detection (heuristics, classifier, graph-based), influence maximization for campaigns, and the growing problem of AI-driven accounts. Students learn to separate coordinated from correlated but independent behavior - the central methodological challenge of this field.
core_concepts: Bot detection: features, classifiers, graph signals
LLM-generated accounts and 'AI slop' at scale
learning_outcomes: C3 Apply heuristics/classifiers to detect likely automation
C4 Detect coordinated posting clusters and characterize campaigns
C5 Evaluate false-positive risk when accusing accounts
methods_models: Feature engineering (posting regularity, entropy, device patterns), clustering on synchronization features, greedy influence maximization, anomaly detection
evaluation_metrics: Precision/recall/F1 on labelled bot sets (Botometer-style), cluster quality (silhouette, purity), false-positive rate on hand-checked samples
pitfalls_limitations: Labelling automation as intent; deleted/hidden accounts; synchronized activity being explainable by platform prompts; accusing real users; model drift against evasion
tools_stack: python-igraph/networkx, scikit-learn, community detection, Botometer API (availability varies), temporal clustering tools
commercial_platforms: Brief mention of commercial bot-detection and brand-safety tools
tools_access_cost: Some detection services are paid; the algorithmic approaches are free to implement
lab_activities: Detect coordinated clusters in a topic network and write a careful, defensible report with false-positive caveats
datasets_apis: Public bot/bot-like labelled datasets (botometer-adjacent), topic networks
assessment_methods: Lab notebook plus graph figures and a short interpretation; graded on correctness of metrics and defensibility of substantive claims
data_collection_workflow: Build the interaction graph from collected data -> deduplicate accounts and edges -> compute metrics -> cluster communities -> archive graph object and code
textbooks: Zafarani et al., Social Media Mining, ch. on bots
key_papers: 2024-2026 work on LLM-driven coordinated behavior and on AI agents spreading propaganda
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: coordinated behavior increasingly LLM-generated and agent-driven, which breaks classical automation detectors and pushes graph/temporal methods forward
industry_relevance: Used in disinformation/trust-and-safety teams, political-communication research units, community-management analytics, and influence-marketing measurement; network metrics are standard deliverables in crisis-mapping briefings.
localization_context: Practised on Indonesian case networks (election-issue discussion, anti-hoax communities, local brand mentions) where the platform mix and language mix differ from US/EU benchmark datasets.
ethics_regulation: Re-identification risk of pseudonymous accounts, doxxing risk when publishing ego-networks, and the ethical line between mapping influence and surveilling individuals; UU PDP applies to any data tied to identifiable accounts.
case_study_scenarios: Assess whether a public issue's spike on X shows signs of coordinated amplification.
deliverable_format: Coordination analysis notebook + cautious evidence report
